whatItDoes: A browser explorable that models Skyhook's construction-baseline tether as two materials (HMPE bulk plus a 20 km Zylon lower tip; each arm is 320 km). It uses a closed-form piecewise erf form of the uniform-working-stress taper and sizes the HMPE three ways: the canon rule, (1−derate)/SF = 28 % of break; a 20 % cap on every load, which is DECISION_LOG item 10's reading; and a 20 % cap only between catches, when the tips are bare. Results at the baseline are 122.56×, 454.78× (+1,661 t at 5,000 kg) and 212.11× respectively. For each case the page shows the load along the arm with a payload aboard and between catches, a curve of mass against PBO added at either end of the arm, a which-end table, and item 10's '~41× to order ~800×' sentence recomputed in terms of the load fraction f. It refuses rather than substituting a number whenever the canon, the SK99 density line, the layout line or the cap line is missing.
testsPin:
twenty.test.mjs has 18 tests. The external pins are:
- All five mass-ratio rungs and their tonnages in the snapshot of params/rev_a.json (40.32 / 64.30 / 121.83 / 295.27 / 3085.95), reproduced by the all-PBO limit within 5e-4 (Skyhook's own tolerance, tests/test_rev_a_physics.py:180-185), in all three rules and both layouts.
- Skyhook's own physics/skyhook_physics.py, run under python3 -I -B on the snapshot. Its characteristic_velocity_kms and integrated_mass_ratio match the kernel to 1e-12 at 36 grid points each for Zylon and for SK99. This includes the proposal's 122.6 and 488.1.
- CPython math.erf / math.erfc on [0, 6].
- An independent RK4 integration of the tension ODE, with the sizing rules written as a max of areas, over 48 configurations; the worst difference is 5.6e-9.
- Closed forms: tension continuity, the area step σP/σH, the between-catch crossing u*, the hub fraction f(1−e^{−X²}), and the marginal-cost formula checked by finite differences.
- Idea 15's published 484.06 / 1104.53 / 3515.24.
- The 27 quoted doc lines, verbatim at their line numbers via git show 34935cb.
- The sha256 values recorded in the sidecars.
- No canon number typed into model.js, app.js or index.html, and the README tagline and table equal to the computed values.

findingsAboutSourceRepo:
All read at Skyhook 34935cb.

1. docs/DECISION_LOG.md:72 (the same text is in docs/research/mp001_market_pricing.md:46 and docs/program_manifest.md:65) says "Reaching 20% sustained load would require SF ≈ 5 … from ~41× to order ~800×". SF 5 gives 20 % only if the derate is left out of sizing. With the canon's 30 % derate, 20 % is SF 3.5, and SF 5 means 14 %. Either way the 20 % tether is 484.06× (Zylon) or 488.14× (SK99), which is 12.0× the 40.32× rung, not about 20×. 800× corresponds to f = 18.07 % (SF 5 at a 9.67 % derate). Idea 15 first reported the 484.06×; the f framing, SF 3.5 and 18.07 % are new here.

2. docs/DECISION_LOG.md:70 calls the 28–40 % a "steady centrifugal load … genuinely sustained". The 28 % is the load with a payload aboard, which lasts half a rotation (6.7 min) per catch. The arm's own weight is about 95 % of the hub tension and zero at the tip. Between catches, with bare tips, the HMPE hub carries 26.6 %, and the outer 24 % of an all-HMPE arm is below 20 %.

3. docs/DECISION_LOG.md:74, outcome (b), says "boundary shifted toward PBO for the high-stress fraction". Under the canon's uniform-stress taper, every metre of a fibre runs at the same fraction, so there is no high-stress fraction while a payload is aboard. One exists only between catches, and it is at the hub: the opposite end from the baseline's Zylon tip (docs/project_instructions.md:108). Under item 10's own reading the PBO belongs at the tip end; under the between-catch reading it belongs at the hub end.

4. params/rev_a.json has no SK99 density (:71 gives the strength only; idea 15 also found this) and no hybrid layout length (:69 says only "Zylon outer arm"). The canon's ladder is an all-Zylon tether, while the baseline is 97 % HMPE by length; at equal load fraction that changes the mass by only +0.6 %.

5. Three different HMPE grades are named for one role: Spectra (rev_a.json:69, the bulk fibre), Dyneema SK99 (rev_a.json:71, the canon strength) and SK78 (DECISION_LOG.md:70, the creep guidance).

Also: the TP-001 creep series has no protocol anywhere in the checkout, and ST-002 (mp001_market_pricing.md:48) hangs coupons at constant loads only.
deviationsFromProposal:
1. The SK99 density of 970 kg/m³ is NOT in rev_a.json, as the proposal claimed. It comes from docs/project_instructions.md:67 (founding doc), corroborated by mp001:22. It is parsed from a snapshot of that line, every HMPE-dependent number is flagged 'ρ not canon', and SK99 is refused if the line is missing or reworded.

2. The proposal's three controls (boundary, f_H, f_P) became:
- PBO added per arm from the §4.1 baseline, at the tip end or the hub end
- one working load for both fibres (the canon has one SF and one derate)
- a cap
- a rule: canon / cap on every load / cap between catches
- tip mass between catches (β)
- a fibre selector with a custom, user-entered HMPE

The proposal's two curves are the 'canon' and 'every' curves. The 'between catches' rule, the hub-end layout and β are additions, made because the between-catch load turned out to be the substantive finding.

3. The boundary is applied to the asymmetric §4.1 baseline (Zylon tip only on the lower arm), not to a symmetric single boundary. The single-fibre limits are tested through the kernel directly.

4. 'Length above the 20 % line is simply the HMPE share' is confirmed with a payload aboard, but the strip also shows the between-catch state, where it is not.

5. The SF 5 figures (484/1105/3515) are kept but reframed as three different load fractions (20/17/14 %). Idea 15 is credited for 484.06.

6. The 1e5-point quadrature test became an RK4 ODE integration over 48 configurations.

7. Item 10's '~800×' is reported as a discrepancy, with the f that would produce it.
notBuilt:
1. No creep model, lifetime or replacement cadence (outcome a). There is no creep law in the repo and fiber_cost_per_kg is null.
2. No DM20 curve (outcome c). The repo gives only a ">50×" ratio, with no strength or density.
3. The 'cap between catches' rule is computed exactly, but whether HMPE creep actually allows it (a steady load with periodic 6.7-minute excursions to 28 %) cannot be proven from the repo. The README labels this [Speculative].
4. Gravity gradient, catch transients, joints and tip-vehicle mass are not modelled; β = 0 is a lower bound, not an estimate.
5. Only two layout families are explored (PBO added at the tip end or at the hub end). Three-section arms and stepped tapers are not.
6. The kernel has not been through Skyhook's Rule 1 review, a VM entry, or the pytest suite (pytest is not installed).
7. Nothing is priced.
